lines.text: Poison, in a frown? In theory, a banknote's weight could kill a million people.
lines.phonemes: pˈɔɪzən, ɪn ɐ fɹˈaʊn? ɪn θˈiəɹi, ɐ bˈaŋknəʊtz wˈeɪt kʊd kˈɪl ɐ mˈɪliən pˈiːpəl.

lines.text: Every frown starts at a nerve ending, letting out a chemical messenger onto the muscle below. The muscle pulls, and the skin above folds into a crease.
lines.phonemes: ˈɛvɹɪ fɹˈaʊn stˈɑːts atə nˈɜːv ˈɛndɪŋ, lˈɛtɪŋ ˈaʊt ɐ kˈɛmɪkəl mˈɛsɪndʒəɹ ˌɒntʊ ðə mˈʌsəl bɪlˈəʊ. ðə mˈʌsəl pˈʊlz, and ðə skˈɪn əbˌʌv fˈəʊldz ˌɪntʊ ɐ kɹˈiːs.

lines.text: Botulinum toxin never touches the skin. It slips inside the nerve ending and cuts one protein the message needs, so the message waits, and never leaves.
lines.phonemes: bˌɒtjʊlˈaɪnəm tˈɒksɪn nˈɛvə tˈʌtʃɪz ðə skˈɪn. ɪt slˈɪps ɪnsˈaɪd ðə nˈɜːv ˈɛndɪŋ and kˈʌts wˈɒn pɹˈəʊtiːn ðə mˈɛsɪdʒ nˈiːdz, sˌəʊ ðə mˈɛsɪdʒ wˈeɪts, and nˈɛvə lˈiːvz.

lines.text: Two centuries ago a German doctor, Justinus Kerner, traced a deadly paralysis to spoiled sausages, and guessed the same poison might one day become a medicine.
lines.phonemes: tˈuː sˈɛntʃəɹiz ɐɡˈəʊ ɐ dʒˈɜːmən dˈɒktə, jʊstˈiːnʊs kˈɛɐnɐ , tɹˈeɪst ɐ dˈɛdli pəɹˈaləsˌɪs tə spˈɔɪld sˈɒsɪdʒɪz, and ɡˈɛst ðə sˈeɪm pˈɔɪzən mˌaɪt wˈɒn dˈeɪ bɪkˌʌm ɐ mˈɛdsən.

lines.text: A dose of this medicine isn't weighed; it's counted in mouse deaths. One frown takes twenty of those, still under a hundredth of what could kill a person.
lines.phonemes: ɐ dˈəʊs ɒv ðɪs mˈɛdsən ˌɪzənt wˈeɪd; ɪts kˈaʊntɪd ɪn mˈaʊs dˈɛθs. wˈɒn fɹˈaʊn tˈeɪks twˈɛnti ɒv ðˈəʊz, stˈɪl ˌʌndəɹ ɐ hˈʌndɹədθ ɒv wɒt kʊd kˈɪl ɐ pˈɜːsən.

lines.text: And the gap that message never crosses is about two thousand times thinner than a sheet of paper.
lines.phonemes: and ðə ɡˈap ðat mˈɛsɪdʒ nˈɛvə kɹˈɒsɪz ɪz ɐbˌaʊt tˈuː θˈaʊzənd tˈaɪmz θˈɪnə ðˌanə ʃˈiːt ɒv pˈeɪpə.

lines.text: Poison in a frown: one message silenced, and months later the nerve grows spare endings, then prunes them away.
lines.phonemes: pˈɔɪzən ɪn ɐ fɹˈaʊn: wˈɒn mˈɛsɪdʒ sˈaɪlənst, and mˈʌnθs lˈeɪtə ðə nˈɜːv ɡɹˈəʊz spˈeəɹ ˈɛndɪŋz, ðˈɛn pɹˈuːnz ðˌɛm ɐwˈeɪ.

lines.text: Next: two neighbours under the same sun, one experiment. Which hand aged?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: tˈuː nˈeɪbəz ˌʌndə ðə sˈeɪm sˈʌn, wˈɒn ɛkspˈɛɹɪmənt. wˌɪtʃ hˈand ˈeɪdʒd?
